Fixture: 82_alpha_vardct_rgba_64x64_nofilters.jxl
64x64 RGBA, VarDCT lossy d=1.0, filters off, 8-bit colour and 8-bit alpha

Purpose
-------
Wave 6 rung 3 and the wave's target construct: an extra channel in a kVarDCT
frame. A kVarDCT frame has no modular colour channels at all, so before this
wave its G.1.3 GlobalModular row was an empty sub-bitstream (H.1 reads nothing
for zero channels) and its LfGroup/PassGroup modular rows read nothing either.
With one extra channel present all three rows become live, interleaved into
sections otherwise full of VarDCT structures. At 64x64 the alpha channel fits
inside group_dim, so this rung isolates the GlobalModular arm.

Frame structure, as parsed by JPXL itself (jpxl-decode's own frame-header
reader, not by any oracle):

  frame 0  kRegularFrame  kVarDCT  1 group, 1 LF group, 1 TOC section
           1 extra channel (kAlpha), ec_upsampling 1, dim_shift 0

The colour content is the shape the VarDCT and progressive recipes use -- a
smooth left half and a 1-pixel checkerboard right half, the highest spatial
frequency a discrete grid can represent, so cjxl's own transform-selection
heuristic reaches for a mixture of varblock sizes. This sidecar does not claim
particular transforms were chosen.

The alpha content is deliberately NOT the same shape as the colour: a radial
ramp with a hard-edged fully transparent notch in the top-left quadrant. A
decode that transposed the alpha plane with a colour plane, shifted it, or
dropped it and left zeros therefore cannot produce a plausible image, and the
test asserts the alpha plane is non-constant before it grades anything.

Grading (18181-3 4.2)
---------------------
--gaborish=0 --epf=0 disables both restoration filters. Per 18181-3 Annex A
Table A.1 that puts the stream in the tighter error class:

    Part 3 error class:  peak <= 0.004,  RMSE <= 1e-5   (no filters)

The alpha channel is graded separately and more strictly: cjxl codes the extra
channel losslessly at these settings, so its peak error must stay at the f32
round-trip level (1e-6), which the lossy colour budget could otherwise hide.

Grading is against a reference DECODE of this stream (the committed .npy, or a
fresh djxl decode), never against the original source PNG -- Part 3 conformance
bounds decoder-vs-reference error, not encoder loss against the pre-encode
image.

  Fixture:      2923 bytes
                sha256 164b7ffb6097e3e089fddf15a9290002e4b8ed9a6072d7661b9ba733f7263c33

  Reference decode (djxl --output_format npy):
    82_alpha_vardct_rgba_64x64_nofilters.npy  (65614 bytes)
    sha256 e106f0ff96d7344baaf423ee9ad9bdb0712cfe73601373fff8c6b4ce51146143
    Committed alongside the fixture (< 100 KB).
    Shape (1, 64, 64, 4) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2. The channel count
    includes the alpha channel: djxl interleaves the extra channels after the
    colour ones, which is the same order G.1.3 gives the modular channel list
    and the order jpxl-decode returns its planes in. Readable with
    jpxl_conformance::FloatImage::from_npy.
    Regenerable at any time from the fixture with the pinned djxl build
    (decode is deterministic per libjxl revision, see PINNED_REVISIONS.txt).

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
